We compare the Monte Carlo (MC) method with nonparametric bootstrapping (NB) using the simple mediation model with complete data.
One advantage of MC over NB is speed.
This is because the model is only fitted once in MC whereas it is fitted many times in NB.


``` r
library(package = semmcci)
library(package = lavaan)
library(package = microbenchmark)
```

## Data


``` r
n <- 1000
a <- 0.50
b <- 0.50
cp <- 0.25
s2_em <- 1 - a^2
s2_ey <- 1 - cp^2 - a^2 * b^2 - b^2 * s2_em - 2 * cp * a * b
em <- stats::rnorm(n = n, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(x = s2_em))
ey <- stats::rnorm(n = n, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(x = s2_ey))
X <- stats::rnorm(n = n)
M <- a * X + em
Y <- cp * X + b * M + ey
df <- data.frame(X, M, Y)
```

## Model Specification

The indirect effect is defined by the product of the slopes
of paths `X` to `M` labeled as `a` and `M` to `Y` labeled as `b`.
In this example, we are interested in the confidence intervals of `indirect`
defined as the product of `a` and `b` using the `:=` operator
in the `lavaan` model syntax.


``` r
model <- "
  Y ~ cp * X + b * M
  M ~ a * X
  X ~~ X
  indirect := a * b
  direct := cp
  total := cp + (a * b)
"
```

## Model Fitting

We can now fit the model using the `sem()` function from `lavaan`.


``` r
fit <- lavaan::sem(data = df, model = model)
```

## Monte Carlo Confidence Intervals

The `fit` `lavaan` object can then be passed to the `MC()` function from `semmcci`
to generate Monte Carlo confidence intervals.


``` r
MC(lav = fit, R = 100L, alpha = 0.05)
#> Monte Carlo Confidence Intervals
#>             est     se   R   2.5%  97.5%
#> cp       0.2333 0.0296 100 0.1806 0.2903
#> b        0.5082 0.0279 100 0.4555 0.5527
#> a        0.4820 0.0280 100 0.4220 0.5301
#> X~~X     1.0590 0.0426 100 0.9883 1.1428
#> Y~~Y     0.5462 0.0231 100 0.5064 0.5959
#> M~~M     0.7527 0.0337 100 0.6846 0.8029
#> indirect 0.2449 0.0179 100 0.2058 0.2738
#> direct   0.2333 0.0296 100 0.1806 0.2903
#> total    0.4782 0.0295 100 0.4162 0.5283
```

## Nonparametric Bootstrap Confidence Intervals

Nonparametric bootstrap confidence intervals can be generated in `lavaan` using the following.


``` r
lavaan::parameterEstimates(
  object = lavaan::sem(
    data = df,
    model = model,
    se = "bootstrap",
    bootstrap = 100L
  )
)
#>        lhs op      rhs    label   est    se      z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#> 1        Y  ~        X       cp 0.233 0.025  9.395      0    0.183    0.278
#> 2        Y  ~        M        b 0.508 0.028 18.057      0    0.454    0.568
#> 3        M  ~        X        a 0.482 0.026 18.550      0    0.433    0.535
#> 4        X ~~        X          1.059 0.046 23.224      0    0.969    1.161
#> 5        Y ~~        Y          0.546 0.023 23.640      0    0.508    0.593
#> 6        M ~~        M          0.753 0.033 23.131      0    0.692    0.814
#> 7 indirect :=      a*b indirect 0.245 0.020 12.443      0    0.209    0.289
#> 8   direct :=       cp   direct 0.233 0.025  9.395      0    0.183    0.278
#> 9    total := cp+(a*b)    total 0.478 0.027 17.966      0    0.418    0.518
```

## Benchmark

### Arguments





|Variables |Values |Notes                               |
|:---------|:------|:-----------------------------------|
|R         |1000   |Number of Monte Carlo replications. |
|B         |1000   |Number of bootstrap samples.        |






``` r
benchmark_complete_01 <- microbenchmark(
  MC = {
    fit <- lavaan::sem(
      data = df,
      model = model
    )
    MC(
      lav = fit,
      R = R,
      decomposition = "chol",
      pd = FALSE
    )
  },
  NB = lavaan::sem(
    data = df,
    model = model,
    se = "bootstrap",
    bootstrap = B
  ),
  times = 10
)
```

### Summary of Benchmark Results


``` r
summary(object = benchmark_complete_01, unit = "ms")
#>   expr        min         lq       mean     median         uq        max neval
#> 1   MC   22.63089   22.81256   24.25483   23.07962   24.78608   31.17024    10
#> 2   NB 5273.42917 5321.14108 5352.63667 5353.55207 5385.59964 5450.64806    10
```

### Summary of Benchmark Results Relative to the Faster Method


``` r
summary(object = benchmark_complete_01, unit = "relative")
#>   expr      min       lq     mean   median       uq      max neval
#> 1   MC   1.0000   1.0000   1.0000   1.0000   1.0000   1.0000    10
#> 2   NB 233.0191 233.2549 220.6833 231.9601 217.2832 174.8671    10
```

## Benchmark - Monte Carlo Method with Precalculated Estimates




``` r
fit <- lavaan::sem(
  data = df,
  model = model
)
benchmark_complete_02 <- microbenchmark(
  MC = MC(
    lav = fit,
    R = R,
    decomposition = "chol",
    pd = FALSE
  ),
  NB = lavaan::sem(
    data = df,
    model = model,
    se = "bootstrap",
    bootstrap = B
  ),
  times = 10
)
```

### Summary of Benchmark Results


``` r
summary(object = benchmark_complete_02, unit = "ms")
#>   expr         min         lq        mean      median          uq         max
#> 1   MC    3.352526    3.41363    3.696643    3.465072    3.545688    5.253109
#> 2   NB 5162.889921 5189.26185 5212.519184 5208.775921 5226.892567 5271.628841
#>   neval
#> 1    10
#> 2    10
```

### Summary of Benchmark Results Relative to the Faster Method


``` r
summary(object = benchmark_complete_02, unit = "relative")
#>   expr  min       lq     mean   median       uq      max neval
#> 1   MC    1    1.000    1.000    1.000    1.000    1.000    10
#> 2   NB 1540 1520.159 1410.068 1503.223 1474.155 1003.526    10
```
